extracted.intended_audience: Investigators applying for NIGMS MIRA (R35) grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program-level requirements for investigators (established, new, and early-stage) applying to the NIGMS Maximizing Investigators' Research Award (MIRA, R35) funding mechanism. Covers eligibility categories, NOFO/application windows, and program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research within NIGMS mission
rubrics_metrics.description: MIRA provides support for research in an investigator's laboratory that falls within the mission of NIGMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must propose research that is within the NIGMS mission; see program NOFOs and mission statements linked on the page for scope details. Contacts are provided for questions about mission fit (NIGMS_EINIMIRA@nigms.nih.gov for EIs/NIs; NIGMS-ESIMIRA@nigms.nih.gov for ESIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant duration
rubrics_metrics.description: MIRA grants will generally be for 5 years for established investigators, new investigators, and early-stage investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Generally’ indicates the standard award period; applicants should consult the specific PAR/NOFO for any exceptions or precise award dates and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Established Investigators (EIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Established investigators eligible for MIRA include those who currently hold an NIGMS R01-equivalent grant or who wish to renew a MIRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program has been expanded (see PAR-26-121) to include these established investigators. Applicants should review PAR-26-121 and contact NIGMS_EINIMIRA@nigms.nih.gov (Ashley Barnes, Ph.D.; Baishali Maskeri, Ph.D.) for specific eligibility questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — New Investigators (NIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: New investigators are eligible provided they are not serving as a subproject leader on any multicomponent awards and propose research that falls within the NIGMS mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to PAR-26-121 for details. New investigators who are subproject leaders on multicomponent awards are excluded; applicants should verify status and review NOFO language and contact program staff with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — Early Stage Investigators (ESIs) and required application pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Early stage investigators should apply through the ESI-specific PAR/NOFO (PAR-23-145) rather than the EI/NI PAR; NIH definitions and policies for ESIs apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'PAR-23-145 - Applications accepted through February 3, 2026' and the NIH page on definitions/policies for Early Stage Investigators. Also see forecast announcement PAR-26-032 for ESI MIRA. Contact NIGMS-ESIMIRA@nigms.nih.gov (Michelle R. Bond, Ph.D.; Marc Rigas, Ph.D.) for ESI questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOFO/application windows and identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific PAR/NOFOs govern application acceptance windows and applicant eligibility for different investigator categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAR-26-121 covers MIRA for established and new investigators (applications accepted in 2026–2028). PAR-23-145 covers MIRA for ESIs (applications accepted through Feb 3, 2026). PAR-26-032 is a forecast announcement for ESIs. Applicants must follow the applicable PAR/NOFO for deadlines and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MIRA program goals and selection priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The MIRA program's goals are to increase the efficiency of NIGMS funding, provide investigators greater stability and flexibility, enhance scientific productivity and the chances for important breakthroughs, and distribute funding more widely among highly talented and promising investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These program objectives contextualize why MIRA exists and may inform programmatic priorities when NIGMS evaluates and funds applications; applicants should frame proposals to align with these aims (stability/flexibility, productivity, broad distribution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for administrative supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: There is specific guidance on whether and how MIRA awards are eligible for administrative supplements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the linked 'MIRA Eligibility for Administrative Supplements' guidance on the page for criteria, allowable uses, and application instructions for supplements to existing MIRA awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant resources and informational materials
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS provides multiple resources to help applicants prepare MIRA applications, including FAQs, an eligibility decision tree, applicant slides, virtual office hours, and feedback loop posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult the listed resources (MIRA Welcome Letter; FAQs for PAR-22-180, PAR-23-145; EI/NI and ESI applicant slides; decision tree; virtual office hours) to clarify eligibility, application strategy, and program expectations prior to preparing/submitting an application.
